title: Core signer-first service-to-deployment flow
description: Reconstructed PSTF feature for Bahia's core public service-to-deployment journey. Current repo evidence verifies relay-backed shared state plus signer-first public commands for service creation, deployment intent creation, approval, and deployment history/detail visibility. Human decision capture on 2026-05-05 changed the approved intended behavior in two important ways: successful service creation must hydrate the `/services` list immediately, and deployment policy preview must become a required gate before deployment intent creation. Because current implementation and active tests still encode the older eventual/advisory behavior, this slice now requires follow-up rather than remaining fully verified.
dependencies: `/api/v1/system/info` must advertise `features.relay_read_models`, at least one public browser relay, and a Bahia service pubkey for canonical read-model filtering.
The shared browser control-plane bootstrap must connect to public relays, query until EOSE, and keep live subscriptions open.
Signer-first public request publication depends on `web/src/lib/nostr/controlplane-requests.js`, accepted relay publishes, and correlated result events.
Bahia request handling depends on the canonical control-plane kinds documented in `docs/control-planes.md` and `docs/nostr-commands.md`.
Browser-visible deployment history and pending approvals depend on Bahia-authored replaceable read models for services, environments, deployment intents, and deployment runs.

actors.name: authenticated_signer
actors.role: browser requester that signs public service and deployment commands

actors.name: bahia_service
actors.role: advertises discovery metadata, validates public commands, and publishes correlated results plus replaceable read models

actors.name: public_browser_relays
actors.role: carry canonical read models and signer-first public request/result traffic for this slice

in_scope: relay-backed bootstrap of services, environments, artifacts, builds, deployment intents, and deployment runs
signer-first public service creation from `/services` via kind `5964` and correlated result handling
deployment policy preview from `/services/[id]` via kind `5989`
signer-first deployment intent creation from `/services/[id]` via kind `5961`
signer-first deployment approval and rejection from `/deployments/pending` via kind `5966`
deployment history and deployment detail rendering from relay-backed public read models on `/deployments` and `/deployments/[id]`
out_of_scope: service secrets, notifications, payments, orgs, and other encrypted request domains
treating mounted REST write endpoints as the approved contract for this slice

docs: `docs/control-planes.md` and `docs/nostr-commands.md` agree that the canonical public deployment flow uses signed kinds `5964`, `5989`, `5961`, and `5966`, with correlated `796x` results and relay-backed read models rather than polling.

`pstf/product_map.md` identifies this slice as a candidate core product identity flow, while `pstf/spec_gap_report.md` warns that transport expectations must be explicit because Bahia mixes relay-backed and REST compatibility surfaces.

The planning docs do not explicitly settle whether service-create success must immediately hydrate the service list or whether policy preview is mandatory versus advisory; those decisions were captured via HITL on 2026-05-05.
code: `internal/api/handlers/system.go` advertises relay-read-model capability and service pubkey discovery consumed by the browser bootstrap path.

`web/src/lib/stores/index.svelte.js` routes `loadServices`, `loadEnvironments`, `loadArtifacts`, `loadBuilds`, and `loadDeploymentIntents` through shared relay bootstrap rather than REST list endpoints.
`web/src/lib/stores/public-controlplane.svelte.js` implements signer-first public command helpers for service create, deployment intent create, approval/rejection, and policy evaluation.
`web/src/routes/services/+page.svelte` creates services through signer-first requests and then calls `loadServices()`, but does not add a created row locally or force a projection refresh.

`web/src/routes/services/[id]/+page.svelte` treats policy preview as best-effort UX today: preview failures do not block `handleDeploy()`, and the modal text explicitly says backend enforcement remains authoritative.
`web/src/routes/deployments/+page.svelte` and `/deployments/pending/+page.svelte` now derive rendered state reactively from the shared relay-backed store.
tests: `web/tests/unit/controlplane-store.test.js` proves discovery-driven relay bootstrap, EOSE-bounded catch-up, canonical-author filtering, replaceable latest-wins behavior, and live subscription continuity.

`web/tests/unit/public-controlplane.test.js` proves signer-first command shaping for service create, policy evaluate, deployment intent create, and deployment approval, including correlated terminal error propagation.

`web/tests/e2e/service-deployment-public-smoke.spec.js` proves a browser journey that publishes kinds `5964`, `5989`, `5961`, and `5966`, renders relay-backed deployment history/detail state, and avoids encrypted request kind `5980`.
The active E2E does not currently assert immediate post-create list hydration, and it traces policy preview publication but not preview-as-gate behavior.
issues_or_bugs: `bahia-xl4y` tracks PSTF work for this slice and now needs follow-up because the approved intended behavior exceeds the currently verified implementation.
existing_behavior: The currently verified product behavior is a signer-first public flow with eventual relay-backed state convergence and advisory policy preview UX.
Two route-level reactivity bugs on `/deployments` and `/deployments/pending` were previously fixed and are reflected in the active verification artifacts.

summary: The browser loads shared system info, resolves public relays plus the Bahia service pubkey, queries canonical read models until EOSE, and then stays subscribed for live updates.
`/services` creates a service by publishing kind `5964`, awaiting a correlated `7963` result, closing the modal, and then calling `loadServices()`.
`loadServices()` is just shared relay bootstrap; it does not guarantee a fresh service projection beyond the normal relay-backed eventual consistency path.
`/services/[id]` requests policy preview through kind `5989`, but preview failure only shows a warning and does not block deployment intent creation.
`/services/[id]` creates deployment intents through kind `5961` with `service`, `environment`, and `artifact` tags.
`/deployments/pending` approves or rejects pending intents through kind `5966`, and the pending/history pages update reactively from the relay-backed store.
The current browser slice uses public request kinds only; the active E2E explicitly excludes encrypted request kind `5980`.

questionable_or_legacy_behavior.behavior: Service-create success does not currently prove or guarantee immediate `/services` list hydration in the same session.
Policy preview is currently advisory and non-blocking even when preview fails, which is now below the approved product intent.

summary: This slice is intended to remain signer-first and event-driven: the browser bootstraps from relay read models, publishes signed public commands, and follows correlated Nostr results rather than REST CRUD responses or polling loops.

Successful service creation must produce user-visible immediate hydration on `/services` after the signer-first create command succeeds; waiting for a later incidental projection without reflecting the created service is not acceptable as the approved experience.

Deployment policy preview is an approved required gate for deployment intent creation in this slice. The browser must obtain a successful preview before allowing intent creation, and preview blockers must stop the request instead of merely warning.
Deployment intent creation and approval remain authoritative signer-first public request/result flows using kinds `5961` and `5966` plus correlated public results.
Deployment history, pending approvals, and deployment detail must continue deriving state from Bahia-authored relay-backed read models and remain reactive to later projections.
Encrypted request kind `5980` remains outside this core public slice.

preconditions: The browser has an authenticated signer session.
`/api/v1/system/info` advertises `relay_read_models`, at least one public browser relay URL, and a Bahia service pubkey.
Public browser relays are reachable and accept relay-backed read-model subscriptions.
The requester pubkey is authorized for the public command families it invokes.
postconditions: Core service and deployment commands complete through correlated public Nostr result events rather than REST write responses.
The `/services` page reflects a successful created service immediately after command success in the same user session.
The deployment modal does not create an intent unless policy preview succeeded and reported no blocking outcome.
Deployment history and pending approvals remain reactive to relay-backed projection updates.
The approved core slice stays on public request kinds and does not depend on encrypted request kind `5980`.

happy_paths.title: Create a service and see it immediately on the services page
steps: Browser bootstraps shared public read models from the advertised relay set.
User opens the create-service modal on `/services` and submits a valid form.
Frontend publishes kind `5964` and receives a correlated successful `7963` result.
The services page immediately shows the created service without requiring manual refresh or leaving the page.

happy_paths.title: Preview policy, create a deployment intent, and approve it
steps: User opens `/services/[id]` for a service with artifacts and environments.
Frontend requests a successful policy preview through kind `5989` for the selected artifact and environment.
If the preview reports no blockers, frontend publishes kind `5961` and receives a correlated deployment result.
Deployment intent projections appear on history and pending-approval pages.
Frontend publishes kind `5966` for approval or rejection, and updated read models reflect the resulting state.

failure_paths.title: Public request publish rejection
failure_paths.behavior: If no relay accepts a signed public request, the caller must receive the relay rejection reason rather than a false success.

failure_paths.title: Terminal public command error
failure_paths.behavior: If a correlated `796x` result reports `status=error|failed`, the frontend must surface the backend-provided error instead of treating the command as successful.

failure_paths.title: Missing or failed policy preview
failure_paths.behavior: If policy preview cannot be completed successfully, deployment intent creation must stay blocked until preview succeeds or the product requirement is re-decided.

failure_paths.title: Policy preview blockers
failure_paths.behavior: If policy preview reports blockers, the browser must not publish the deployment-intent request.

edge_cases: Public request/result correlation must ignore spoofed replies from non-service authors.
Replaceable read-model bootstrap must prefer latest Bahia-authored events and tombstones by `(kind, pubkey, d-tag)`.
Immediate service hydration may require reconciling a successful terminal result with slower projection arrival; the implementation must still satisfy the approved UX promise.
Deployment history and pending approvals must remain reactive when late-arriving `31967` or run-projection updates arrive after navigation.
non_functional_requirements: The slice must remain Nostr-native and event-driven: no polling loops, timeout-based completion, or REST CRUD fallbacks for the approved public flow.
Bootstrap must remain EOSE-aware and preserve live subscriptions after historical catch-up.
The public deployment slice must stay distinct from encrypted request domains and encrypted relay sets.
Shared browser state must remain canonicalized around Bahia-authored relay events.

contradictions_and_gaps.note: Current `/services` behavior proves signer-first create success but does not prove the newly approved immediate-hydration requirement.
Current deployment modal copy and logic explicitly allow intent creation when policy preview is unavailable, which conflicts with the newly approved gating requirement.
Existing acceptance and verification artifacts for this slice still reflect the older eventual-consistency/advisory-preview stance and need synchronization with the new HITL-approved intent.
